A made-up class under the real class of climate types could exist unrecorded (a newly proposed regional type), and the real Mediterranean rule (more rain in winter) is not contradicted because the new type is not said to be Mediterranean.

notes: TBox expansion, paired with geography-replace-0006. Keeps the revision's relation (rainier_season_in) and new object (summer) and gives them to a made-up class (a vesperine climate, a newly described climate type) under the real class of climate types, so no old value is pushed out and the real Mediterranean rule is untouched. The derived queries name invented places (Velmarrow, Brindelmoor, Quenstead) with the class stated in the prompt (inheritance, 2 hops, bridge in the prompt): the inserted rule is their only route. The third is an application (rainwater tanks). Near unrelated: the rainy season of Athens, a real Mediterranean place, which must stay 'winter' (a leaked 'rain in summer' would change it). Names are invented; the evidence records that they are absent from the corpus. Side facts and checks are those of the paired revision.
